research.comment: The fund invests across the semiconductor value chain. SK Hynix's Q3 2026 results—revenue +328% YoY, operating profit +632% YoY—confirm a massive AI-driven memory cycle. HBM supply remains tight; the company sees shortages persisting through 2030. This signals broad second-order effects for equipment, packaging, and foundry capacity. Archived coverage is limited to headlines/excerpts; full earnings-call transcript text is unavailable due to fetch error. External search dates are publisher metadata, not independent snapshots.

ideas.thesis: SK Hynix posted record Q3 revenue and profit, driven by AI HBM demand; it expects memory shortages through 2030 and has 50%+ 2027–28 output pre-sold to 14 buyers.
ideas.risk: Priced-in after ~8% jump; global macro or AI capex slowdown would hit highly valued memory names.

ideas.thesis: As the dominant AI GPU maker, NVIDIA is a primary consumer of SK Hynix’s HBM; sustained memory shortages through 2030 signal continued explosive AI infrastructure buildout.
ideas.risk: NVIDIA’s own revenue growth depends on timely HBM supply; memory shortages could constrain its AI GPU shipments.

memo.name: Semiconductor fund
memo.criteria: We invest in semiconductors and electronic components across chip designers, foundries, fabrication equipment, memory, advanced packaging and supply chains. Prioritize material changes in chip demand, capacity, revenue, margins, capital spending, manufacturing technology, supply constraints and export restrictions. Both positive and negative developments can create research opportunities. AI or cloud news matters when a concrete connection to chip demand or suppliers is supported. Consumer apps, retail earnings, routine product launches and political stories have low priority without a documented semiconductor transmission. Score the value of researching the news for this mandate, not whether to buy or sell and not its expected return. Distinguish source evidence from speculation and flag limited excerpt coverage.
